A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Blm promotes HR by removing the secondary structures, which are likely to be formed at the recombination sites.
Blm functions in both HR pathways, namely, cross-over and SDSA type HR.
Blm is required for SDSA type HR between diverged segments and that this reaction is essential for the maintenance of genomic stability in higher eukaryotic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Blm is not only an anti-recombingase, but also a recombinase that promotes HR between divergent sequences.
Blm promotes the HR between diverged segments in vertebrates, which is consistent with its function in SDSA in Drosophilla.

Bloom DNA helicases are not anti-recombinases, but rather they are facilitators for homologous recombinations between diverged sequences in vertebrates, which may explain the role of the helicase in the suppression of cancer.
